body: Erika Kirk had a message for conservatives reeling from Republican election setbacks, and she turned to her late husband Charlie’s words to deliver it.
"I miss Charlie so much every single day, but especially on a day like today," she wrote.
"He always said that when things are going well, we need to stay humble. And when things aren’t going the way we want, we need to stay positive, keep our faith, and get back to work."
ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION
The widow of Turning Point USA CEO and founder Charlie Kirk said her husband had built a political operation meant to endure both victories and defeats.

"Charlie’s vision for Turning Point Action was always bigger than one election," she wrote. "He wanted a permanent, year-round operation with the people, relationships, and resources to compete in every cycle.
INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES
"He knew there would be victories and setbacks because he had experienced both and that’s why he built for both."
Kirk also thanked the staff, students, volunteers and ballot chasers who worked during the election cycle.
ERIKA KIRK SAYS PRESIDENTIAL LIBRARY-STYLE TRIBUTE TO CHARLIE KIRK IS 'IN THE WORKS' AS TPUSA EXPANDS
"I know Charlie would be unbelievably proud of each and every one of you, and I am, too," she wrote.

In a lengthy post on X, Erika Kirk said Republicans saw once comfortable races tighten or flip as candidates she described as democratic socialists campaigned on the cost of gas, groceries and housing.
FLORIDA CONGRESSMAN DIAGNOSES GOP'S BLUE TSUNAMI LOSSES: 'WE FAILED TO MAKE THEM THINK WE CARED ABOUT THEM'

"A rising stock market doesn’t mean much when nearly half of Americans don’t have a 401K and just want to put gas in their trucks, put food on the table, and provide a good life for their families," she wrote.
Erika Kirk paired her warning with a defense of free enterprise, arguing conservatives must understand why voters looked elsewhere without embracing the policies their opponents offered.
CALLING DEMOCRATS ‘COMMUNISTS’ WON’T WIN GEN Z — REPUBLICANS NEED A BETTER OFFER
"We can disagree with the solutions voters were offered while still recognizing why they were looking elsewhere for answers," she wrote.
Erika Kirk warned conservatives against turning on one another as she urged them to take voters’ frustrations seriously.
JASON CHAFFETZ: FIVE TIMELESS POLITICAL LESSONS THAT GOT LOST IN 2026

"The biggest mistake conservatives can make right now would be to allow this moment to become another exercise in finger-pointing, in-fighting, or trying to secure their own political preservation," she wrote.
"That does not solve the problems the American people are demanding be solved."
Erika Kirk said exit polls showed voters were concerned about the economy and the war in Iran .
FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: 2026 MIDTERM ELECTIONS USHER IN A BLUE WAVE AS DEMOCRATS WIN CONTROL OF CONGRESS
She said those concerns echoed what Turning Point had been hearing from students around the country for months.
"This isn’t a surprise to us because we’ve heard the same concerns from our students around the country for months and we’ve been concerned about it too," she wrote.
JONATHAN TURLEY: SOCIALISM IS BACK IN STYLE, AND DEMOCRATS ARE BUYING THE PITCH
Erika Kirk rejected socialism as an answer, arguing it places economic power in government hands rather than allowing individuals and families to build prosperity.
She said that approach conflicts with the free enterprise, individual liberty and opportunity at the heart of the country.
But she also warned that Americans will not simply stick with a party out of habit.

"Americans are not looking for labels and don’t subscribe to unquestioned party loyalty anymore either," she wrote. "They will support the candidates who can both speak to their concerns and deliver on what THEY need and dream about for their families."
She identified affordable homes, safe communities and greater opportunity for the next generation as the promises voters want fulfilled.

Erika Kirk said the organization would study the results, listen to voters and spend the next two years making the case that conservative policies and free markets can address the problems Americans face.
She pledged to continue building relationships in communities across the country and preparing for "2028 and beyond."
"Our principles haven’t changed and neither has our mission," she wrote.
"Onward."

articles.headline: 3 stats that prove Wizards' AJ Dybantsa is already on the cusp of NBA stardom
keyFacts: Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa is averaging a league-high 6.3 transition points per game through his first three games.
Dybantsa has recorded a 61.2% true shooting percentage during his limited three-game sample size.
Washington concedes just 99.4 points per 100 possessions during Dybantsa's minutes on the floor.
body: You'll have to forgive Wizards fans for getting a little carried away with how they feel about AJ Dybantsa's future prospects.

The No. 1 pick has only taken part in three games. But he has looked like the franchise's savior in all three, showing signs of his impending world domination one drop-step, one inch-perfect spin and one contested mid-range jumper at a time.

Dybantsa already figures to have inspired fables in the nation's capital. The numbers suggest he might be deserving of that treatment. Here are three figures that show that Dybantsa is nearing NBA greatness (or something like it).
Three stats that prove AJ Dybantsa is already on the cusp of NBA stardom
NBA-best transition points per game
Dybantsa technically can't qualify for the league-lead in any statistical category, as he has only participated in three of Washington's first seven games.

If we relax those qualifiers and squint our eyes a bit, we'd see that Dybantsa actually has been the league's most fearsome transition finisher since making his debut. Dybantsa is averaging 6.3 transition points per game, per HoopsJunkie. That's more than Giannis Antetokounmpo. That's more than Tyrese Maxey. In fact, that's the highest-mark in the league.

Dybantsa's prowess on the break matches with what our eyes tell us about him. He's a gifted athlete who possesses the dexterity, finesse and lateral quickness to leave defenders in precarious positions. With Trae Young serving as Washington's offense's primary gatekeeper, we'd expect Dybantsa to continue to sit near the top of the chart in that category going forward.
Strong true shooting rate

Dybantsa flaunts a 61.2% true shooting percentage through three games, a clip that would see him be considered one of the Wizards most efficient players if he's able to maintain that percentage for the remainder of the year. Three games is a tiny sample size, to be sure. But the way by which Dybantsa gets his baskets appears to be repeatable — he's a maven on fast breaks who has the sort of lateral movement traits that should make help him bend defenses to his will.

There's a sort of malleability to Dybantsa's scoring, particularly in the painted area. He leverages his movement skills to dance beyond defenders and get to the cup. Defenses will adjust in the hope of changing his mode of attack. His free-throw shooting is also likely to dwindle slightly, bringing down his true-shooting rate.

AJ Dybantsa is one of the most gifted drivers & transition scorers in NBA history. The explosiveness, the change in pace, the balance & the footwork is all ridiculous at 6'9". He's already leading the NBA in transition PPG & shooting 59% on all 2Pers with a strong FTR. Freak. https://t.co/Ob0BgJoKly
— Carson Breber (@Carsobi) November 4, 2026

Nevertheless, there's plenty of evidence that suggests Dybantsa continue to find success in and around the painted area. If he were to maintain a true-shooting percentage around 60 percent, that would represent a dazzling mark — just four rookies who scored at least 400 points last season accomplished that feat (Kon Knueppel, Maxime Raynaud, Ryan Kalkbrenner, Collin Murray-Boyles).
Promising defensive metrics

Washington has quietly emerged as one of the league's better defenses in 2026-27, posting the league's eighth-best defensive rating. In Dybantsa's 90 minutes of game action, the Wizards defense is even more intimidating.
Washington is conceding just 99.4 points per 100 possessions in Dybantsa's minutes. That's more than three points lower than the Pistons' league-leading mark.

Now, some caveats. The Hornets are the league's worst offensive team, while the Magic sit at ninth-worst (and that's before considering the team's standing after injuries to Jalen Suggs and Paolo Banchero). The Cavaliers' attack gashed Washington for 121 in Dybantsa's debut, with the BYU product finishing with a +/- of -3.

Still, there's reason for optimism within Washington's ranks. Per Wizards Central's Greg Finberg, opponents are shooting just 35.1% when matched up against Dybantsa. That figure falls to 16.7% when an attempt comes from beyond the arc.

— Hoop Central (@TheHoopCentral) November 3, 2026
There were questions about how Dybantsa's defense would scale in the NBA. He had a tendency to lose focus at times in college, falling victim to more than a few backdoor cuts and late rotations.

Those concerns are still present, to be sure. We'll need a larger sample size to determine whether Dybantsa's defensive instincts have gone up a gear or he has merely benefitted from advantageous scheduling.
But if Dybantsa's defensive exploits are real, it should propel him to the sort of two-way stardom reserved for the sport's greatest wings. That's right where he wants to be.

articles.headline: Snap has more than 30 million paid subscribers across Snapchat+ and other plans
keyFacts: Snap announced more than 30 million paid subscribers across its subscription plans during its third-quarter earnings report.

body: Snap has more than 30 million paid subscribers across Snapchat+ and other plans
Power users seem more than willing to pay for AI-powered effects.

More than 30 million power users are paying for one of Snap's subscription plans, including Snapchat+ and its ad-free "platinum" tier. The company announced the milestone as part of its third-quarter earnings, saying that its non-advertising "other" revenue grew 84 percent compared with last year.

Snap introduced Snapchat+, which offers users bonus features like the ability to see which friends re-watched your Story, in 2022. Since then, the company has added Lens+, a subscription for AI-powered AR effects; Platinum, which eliminates advertising; and paid storage for the app's Memory feature.

The company didn't share a breakdown of subscribers across all the plans, but noted that Lens+ "has grown nearly 600% since January 2026." That growth suggests at least some of Snapchat's users are particularly enthusiastic about the app's AI-powered features, like its AI photo editing feature called AI Photoshoot. "AI-powered features have helped Lens+ exceed our expectations, demonstrating how new creative experiences can drive demand for our paid products," CEO Evan Spiegel said during the company's earnings call.

While Snap isn't as associated with AI as some of its social media peers, it's notable that AI has helped it drive paid subscribers. X revealed earlier this year that it had about 6.3 million paid subscribers across X Premium and Grok.

Subscriptions were a bright spot for Snap. Spiegel said that advertising revenue was growing "below our ambitions" and the company only added 2 million new daily users since last quarter. Snap said that it would focus on reporting monthly active users rather than daily users, beginning in 2027. Snapchat currently has 977 million monthly users.

The company also warned that its legal challenges and "increased regulatory scrutiny on youth-related issues" could affect its prospects. The company is dealing with numerous lawsuits over alleged safety issues and state attorneys general have pushed for Snap to adopt additional safety features following Meta's high-profile settlement.

articles.headline: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
keyFacts: Macronix announced in its earnings report that its production of ROM chips has reached its end and it will decouple from the game industry.
Analyst David Gibson noted that Macronix serves as Nintendo's main memory chip maker for physical game cartridges.
Macronix said ROM production is being crowded out by the production of more lucrative, in-demand memory chips.
body: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs . Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges.

Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance . That could be an issue for Nintendo, which analyst David Gibson notes uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges.

That ROM production—which has shrunk 39 percent in the last year and now represents just 5 percent of Macronix's business—is being crowded out by production of more lucrative, in-demand chips like NOR- and NAND-based memory and eMMCs, the company said. With Macronix's production capacity stuck at 25,000 12-inch wafers a month—and $1.2 billion in planned new capacity taking a year or more to spin up—less profitable ROM chips are taking up wafer space that can earn more through other types of chips.

articles.headline: AI PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress — here’s how they fared
keyFacts: Political groups supporting and opposing the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence Tuesday’s midterm elections with mixed results.
Leading the Future told TechCrunch it plans to keep spending in the 2028 elections to advocate for a single national AI framework.
Guardrails Alliance stated it wants to continue opposing candidates backed by the AI industry to make that funding politically toxic.
body: Political groups both supporting and opposing the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence Tuesday’s midterm elections and shape the future of AI regulation. That spending produced mixed results, with some of the most heavily backed candidates losing their races.

On the industry side, two AI-focused political action committees (PACs) that raised and spent money to influence the elections — American Mission and Building the Future — collectively spent $4.8 million to back South Carolina Senate candidate Darline Graham, who lost. American Mission is the Republican spending arm of Leading the Future (LTF), a broader political group backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and the VC firm Andreessen Horowitz.

American Mission also spent more than $500,000 apiece supporting Republican House candidates Aaron Flint in Montana and Laurie Buckhout in North Carolina, both of whom lost. LTF’s Democratic spending arm, Think Big, had better luck backing Florida Rep. Jared Moskowitz, who won reelection.

Groups advocating for stronger AI safeguards also saw mixed results. Public First, which is backed by Anthropic, supported several Republicans who lost through its affiliated PAC but had more success backing Democratic candidates. It also contributed $3 million to a PAC supporting California state Sen. Scott Wiener, who was leading his race at the time of publication.

Meanwhile, Guardrails Alliance, a group that has sought to make taking money from AI companies a political liability, spent more than $1 million apiece opposing two candidates who lost: California Rep. Jimmy Gomez and Montana’s Aaron Flint. It also spent $300,000 supporting Angela Gonzales-Torres, who defeated Gomez.

It’s difficult to separate the impact of AI-related spending from the broader Democratic wave that swept Tuesday’s elections. Elon Musk, who reportedly poured half a billion dollars into supporting Republicans in the midterms, also saw many of his candidates lose. Indeed, LTF also backed some candidates it believed were likely to win, only to see them lose to the Dems.

For LTF, though, the general election wasn’t the main focus. The group told TechCrunch ahead of Election Day that it thinks primaries (the contests that choose each party’s nominee) are a more effective use of its money, because spending there can build name recognition and help candidates set up AI policy agendas.

LTF spent $27.38 million in the primaries, including $8 million alone on opposing New York Assembly member Alex Bores, who lost his bid for Congress back in June. When deciding whether it’s worth jumping into a general election race, LTF assesses how competitive the race is, whether it thinks spending could make a difference, and whether it should keep its powder dry for future elections.
Charlie Blaettler, political director of Guardrails Alliance, had a different theory for why LTF spent comparatively little in the general election.

“They don’t want their money to become an issue in these elections,” he said. He pointed to the Michigan Senate primary election, in which a pro-Israel lobbying group called AIPAC spent close to $30 million backing Democratic candidate Haley Stevens against Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens conceded the primary to El-Sayed, who went on to win the Senate seat.

“AIPAC became the story in that race,” Blaettler said. “We know people hate AI billionaires. They hate the people running these companies. They’re very distrustful and disgusted by the political spending and lobbying that the tech industry does. If they spend in a competitive race, they would just become an enormous liability for their candidates.”

The main fight among AIPACs, whether they are pro-industry or pro-regulation, is whether Congress should establish a national AI framework that overrides state laws, or whether states will maintain their own ability to impose safeguards.

Neither side seems poised to back down. LTF, which favors a single national AI framework, told TechCrunch it plans to keep spending in the 2028 elections, while Guardrails Alliance says it wants to keep opposing candidates backed by the AI industry.

Blaettler said that while LTF’s ads rarely touch on AI, instead focusing on popular issues for each candidate, Guardrail Alliance’s ads are specifically about who is taking money from the AI industry.
“Our goal is to make AI money politically toxic,” Blaettler said.

articles.headline: How to get Apex Protocol Gear set in The Division 2
keyFacts: Players can obtain the new Apex Protocol Gear set in The Division 2 by playing the Echoes of Central Park DLC.
Players must finish the main story campaign and defeat five bosses known as Guardians located across the map.
Players receive gear pieces as reward loot by damaging and killing the Guardians, with higher difficulties increasing the odds.
body: The Apex Protocol Gear set is a new addition to The Division 2 , and it’s tied directly to the Echoes of Central Park DLC. The DLC has added a new playable area, and you get new bosses to kill.
These bosses are directly involved in providing you with the equipment pieces, but the job is easier said than done.
How to farm Apex Protocol Gear pieces in The Division 2

For starters, you will need to have access to the Echoes of Central Park DLC. Without it, you will not have access to the new location, which is mandatory for farming this gear set. As of writing, there is no other possible way to get the Apex Protocol gear pieces aside from playing in Central Park.

Once you have access to the location, your next task is to finish the main story campaign. It’s a relatively easy one, and you can also finish it as a beginner. Veterans can bring their Prototype gear, but the bonus effects will be unavailable at this location.

Screenshot by Destructoid When you finish the campaign, you will learn about the Guardians . They were all former SHD agents who got involved in nefarious activities. This completely metamorphosed them and turned them into the apex predators. To get your gear pieces, you will need to defeat all of them.

There are five of them located all around the map, and you can see their locations on the image above. Head to the marked spot, and you will find the Lair of a Guardian. Once you reach a lair, you will have to deal enough damage to make the Guardian appear.

You will then have a set amount of time to kill the Guardian. As you deal damage, you will have the possibility of receiving the gear pieces as reward loot. The odds are not listed by Ubisoft, but they certainly go up at higher difficulties in my testing.
Hence, playing at Heroic will be the most rewarding thing if you do not mind the challenge and simply want to increase your luck of finding these pieces of gear.
Image via Ubisoft Here are the bonuses you get from the gear set.
2+ pieces : +10% Weapon Damage, +10% Skill Damage
3+ pieces : +15% Weapon Handling, +15% Hazard Protection
4+ pieces : Apex Engine
Veer Failsafe (backpack talent): Receive +5% armor on kill and +10% skill damage per Apex Engine bonus stack.
Veer Override (chest talent): While at maximum Apex Engine stacks, enemies damaged by your Skills are marked for 10s. Deal +20% Amplified Damage to marked enemies.
The post How to get Apex Protocol Gear set in The Division 2 appeared first on Destructoid .

articles.headline: Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool
keyFacts: Liverpool lost 3-2 to Fenerbahce in the Champions League after conceding three set-piece goals despite leading late in the match.
Manager Andoni Iraola described the conceded goals as cheap and messy, noting that his team failed to secure the victory.
Interim boss Dirk Kuyt led Fenerbahce to the shock comeback victory before stepping aside for incoming head coach Emre Belozoglu.
body: - Published
When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind.
Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win.

But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory.

By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten.
Iraola described the goals they conceded as "cheap" and "messy".

After Liverpool let three points slip from their grasp, Kuyt spoke of how he had encouraged Fenerbahce's players to embrace the never-say-die mindset that allowed the Reds to achieve so many great feats in Europe in the past.
He joined Liverpool in 2006, a year after the team's famous 'Miracle of Istanbul' comeback in the Champions League final, and spent six years as a first-team fixture.
"We told each other to stick together and be united. That's something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against," Kuyt said. "We made a miracle tonight - not many expected us to win."
He and Fenerbahce will remember this one for a long time. Liverpool will want to quickly forget it.
After winning five games in a row, Iraola's side have gone on to lose twice in four days. Arsenal on Sunday, and now this.
On the flight back from Istanbul, there will be plenty of disappointment at the way in which Liverpool failed to see this game out.
"It's frustration because it's a difficult place to come and play," said Iraola. "We were, during most part of the game, thinking we can win this one. But obviously it hasn't happened."
All three of Fenerbahce's goals came from set-pieces.
Two were scored by Englishmen.

Former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood benefited from a slice of luck when his free-kick deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet in the first half for Fenerbahce's first equaliser, and Liverpool only had themselves to blame when Cody Gakpo's header took the ball past Alisson and gave Birmingham-born Archie Brown a tap in to make it 2-2.
Six minutes later, Liverpool made a mess of Brown's looping ball in the box and Vedat Muriqi beat three players in red and headed past Alisson.
"They are cheap goals. They are messy goals," said Iraola.
"It's a free-kick. It's quite far also and it's through the wall.
"Mistakes can cost you. For the last goal, it's a long throw and the first phase is controlled but after a very long ball, Muriqi wins it.
"The second goal, Cody is the one touching the ball just in front of Ali [Alisson].

"In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate because it was so noisy. It was even difficult for me to give any kind of instruction. I suppose the communication between Ali and Cody was difficult."
'They look like they can concede at any moment'
After showing signs of genuine progress in recent weeks, Liverpool let potential victory slip away here in a concerning manner.
Trey Nyoni's first goal for the club had given them an early lead, but the teenager's deflected strike was cancelled out by Greenwood's reply in kind four minutes later.
The real drama came from the 69th minute to the 79th, with Liverpool inching ahead again, close to a fourth win in four in the competition, but unable to see the job through.

"It feels like a step back from what we saw against Arsenal because everyone thought, OK, we are seeing huge improvements from Liverpool," said ex-Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock, who was watching the game for Match of the Day.
"It was a much-changed team. However, the simple mistakes that they made from set-pieces or simple balls into the box are not good enough.

"The frustrating part for Liverpool fans is that we all know what the problems are. So, where is the solution? That's what Iraola is trying to do at the moment, but it's just a question of how long it takes.

"The biggest issue is that this keeps on happening, with Liverpool looking like they can concede at any moment and being so open on the counter-attack. There is a repetitive theme of the goals they are conceding and it undoes all the good work they do when they go forward.
"When you go ahead, twice, away from home at Fenerbahce in the Champions League then, if that is Arsenal they win that game - they see it out against a team like Fenerbahce.
"Liverpool don't have the ability to do that at the moment, and that is what is really frustrating."
'We showed Europe how big Fenerbahce is'
On the eve of this game in the Kadikoy neighbourhood of Istanbul, Kuyt spoke passionately about how Fenerbahce had the opportunity to show Europe their true colours.
He will step aside now, with former Newcastle player Emre Belozoglu taking over as head coach officially from Thursday.
Thanks to this night, Europe now knows all about Fenerbahce.

They have had a torrid season so far, though, having lost four of their 10 league games and taken a 6-0 drubbing at Aston Villa on their travels outside Turkey, but Kuyt's men delivered a performance that will live long in the memory for anyone associated with the club.
"We showed Europe how big Fenerbahce is. This is what the spirit of this side is," said Kuyt.
"I think it's very special that for the first time since 18 years, Fenerbahce win a game against [an English side].
"Some people will remember but the number on the back of my shirt was 18 in Liverpool. So that's something really special for me in person.

"I said exactly the same thing to the players before the game. Although we are in a very difficult situation, we have a chance to bring another miracle in Istanbul. And if you get that miracle, things can change in a positive way."
They delivered in style, with 24-year-old former Derby County prospect Brown getting a goal and an assist in the second half.
"The Champions League is a great opportunity for Archie to show himself," said Kuyt.

"It's well known how good a player he is in Turkey. He did a fantastic job today. His defence and attack were very good. I'm very pleased with his performance, I'm pleased with the performance of all my players.
"It's a very special night for everyone who loves Fenerbahce."

articles.headline: Escape From Tarkov Creator Reveals New Hardcore Sci-Fi Shooter
keyFacts: Escape from Tarkov game director Nikita Buyanov revealed a 14-minute gameplay video for his new sci-fi tactical shooter, Fragmentary Order.
Set in 2251 across the Solar System, the game features players controlling remote clones in large combat zones with familiar extraction shooter mechanics.
Buyanov announced a paid closed testing program called Prime Batch, with the first closed alpha testing wave planned for later this year.
body: Fans of hardcore tactical shooters have a new game to keep an eye on, particularly if they've spent hundreds of hours navigating the brutal world of Escape from Tarkov. Nikita Buyanov, the game director behind the popular extraction shooter, has finally offered a proper look at his next project, and it takes the familiar formula somewhere very different.

Called Fragmentary Order, the upcoming sci-fi tactical shooter just received its first gameplay reveal, featuring 14 minutes of in-engine footage. Set across the Solar System in 2251, the game imagines a future where warfare has become an outsourced business, with players controlling remotely operated clones rather than putting their own lives on the line.
What is Fragmentary Order about?

In Fragmentary Order, players control remotely operated clones known as RepEnts, which are deployed across large combat zones to carry out dangerous missions. Losing one of these clones isn't necessarily the end of the road. In this world, death is simply another business expense, although that doesn't mean players can afford to be careless.

The game features large-scale environments, changing environmental conditions, vehicles, drones, and advanced technological systems. Players will also be able to team up in squads of up to four, with careful coordination and planning playing a major role in surviving encounters.

The gameplay footage also offers a glimpse at looting, inventory management, weapon customization, and firefights that should feel familiar to anyone who has played Escape from Tarkov. It's difficult not to draw comparisons between the two games, although the new project swaps Tarkov's familiar environments for a much more futuristic setting.

Buyanov has ambitious plans for the project, saying in a statement: "We're not building a match you play. We're building a world you live in, for years." He added that he hopes Fragmentary Order will remain just as engaging a decade from now as Escape from Tarkov has been.
Alongside the gameplay reveal, Buyanov announced Prime Batch, a paid closed testing program that gives dedicated players an opportunity to participate in the game's development.
There are two available tiers:
- Candidate ($44.99): Includes access to alpha sessions, major technical playtests, a Candidate ranking designation, and an exclusive in-game package.

- Founder ($79.99): Includes everything in the Candidate tier, along with earlier access to experimental builds, roadmap visibility, a Founder package, and access to a private community with direct developer access.

The first closed alpha testing wave is planned for later this year and will take place under a nondisclosure agreement. However, Fragmentary Order does not yet have a confirmed full release date. For now, fans can watch the 14-minute gameplay showcase and decide whether Buyanov's latest project has what it takes to recreate the appeal of Escape from Tarkov in an entirely different setting.

articles.headline: Viktor Gyökeres the difference as Arsenal claim nervy win against Slavia Prague
keyFacts: Viktor Gyökeres led Arsenal to a narrow win against Slavia Prague with an assist and a goal.
Slavia Prague matched the longest winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history at 23 games after the defeat.
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta admitted his side fell far below their standards during a nervy second half.
body: Another European away day, another victory for Arsenal: albeit only just. This time, Viktor Gyökeres stole the show as poor Slavia Prague matched the longest winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history despite a spirited late comeback. That unwanted record stands at 23, equalling the mark set by AEK Athens and FCSB – formerly known as Steaua Bucharest – while Arsenal are unbeaten in their 10 last away trips.

However, had it not been for a wonder save from David Raya, the Czech champions would have snatched a point after Wiktor Nowak pulled one back late on as Mikel Arteta’s usually watertight defence showed signs of fallibility under pressure.
In contrast to last week’s defeat against Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup, Arsenal had been cruising until the last 15 minutes after Noni Madueke fired them ahead early on, set up superbly by Gyökeres.

That was the Sweden striker’s third assist in his past five appearances, although Arteta will have been even more encouraged by the emphatic finish that appeared to put the game beyond Slavia’s reach just before the break.

But the Arsenal manager admitted his side had taken their eye off the ball by allowing their hosts back into the game with some uncharacteristic defensive lapses as Slavia racked up 18 shots to his side’s 12.

“At half-time, the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game,” said Arteta. “We were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept and in everything that we discussed to avoid the game that we played in the second half. That is a huge learning.”

Slavia’s solitary victory in this competition came in their first-ever match in 2007 and after losing 3-0 to Arsenal here exactly a year ago, they knew their chances of avoiding the unwanted milestone were extremely slim. Arteta’s side have developed a killer instinct on their travels in Europe – not since May 2025 in the second leg of their semi-final against Paris Saint-Germain have Arsenal lost an away game in 90 minutes.

After their exploits at Anfield on Sunday that took them three points clear at the top of the Premier League, Arteta heavily rotated his side again with six changes. It’s perhaps not surprising that Martín Zubimendi ran out of steam given the Spain World Cup winner made only his third start of a so far frustrating campaign.

For the third time in Arsenal’s past four matches, Gyökeres was entrusted with leading the line after finally getting off the mark with a scrappy strike against Fleetwood. He finished as top scorer last season with 21 goals but has clearly been struggling for form and confidence. Yet there was no doubting the quality of his assist for Madueke’s opening goal after just eight minutes.

Raya’s long ball should have been dealt with by the Slavia defence but they made the criminal error of allowing it to bounce. That was the cue for Gyökeres to come alive as he beat his marker to the ball, chested it down and played the perfect pass for the England forward to run on to and score. Arteta’s reaction on the touchline suggested he enjoyed it too.

Mikel Merino was Arsenal’s hero here last year with two goals and he could have extended their lead on three occasions before the half-hour mark. The lively Madueke created his best opportunity after cutting the ball back to Merino but he could not beat Nazar Domchak in Slavia’s goal.

With Martin Ødegaard watching from the bench next to William Saliba on the latter’s return from a long-term back injury, Arsenal lacked some of their usual fluency in attack. But Slavia were still no match for them and their task became almost impossible seven minutes before the break. Gyökeres exchanged a smart one-two with Merino inside the area before curling a brilliant shot into the far corner.

To their credit, the hosts began the second half with much more aggression after introducing their record signing, Ange N’Guessan, from the bench. Ezri Konsa and Declan Rice both found themselves in the book as Arsenal were pinned back. David Jurasek let fly from long range and his effort was deflected just wide of Raya’s goal. From the resulting corner, Gabriel Magalhães somehow managed to clear two goalbound headers off the line in a matter of seconds. The Brazilian celebrated with a massive fist pump but his evening wasn’t over.

Mikulas Konecny should have done much better with another header before Raya managed to push Oskar Kubiak’s header on to the post despite being at full stretch in mid-air. Slavia eventually scored the goal all their endeavour deserved in the final minute of normal time when Nowak fired in at the far post. There were a few nervous moments in stoppage time as Konecny forced Raya into another save. Arteta breathed a sigh of relief at the full-time whistle as Slavia were condemned to their fate.

articles.headline: 'Sloppy' Arsenal survive second-half scare to beat Slavia Prague
keyFacts: Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1 in the UEFA Champions League after first-half goals from Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres.
Manager Mikel Arteta described his team's second-half performance as very sloppy as Slavia Prague mounted a strong comeback.
The victory moved Arsenal up to third in the Champions League league phase table.
body: Slavia Prague vs Arsenal; UEFA Champions League
Slavia Prague vs Arsenal. UEFA Champions League.
Eden Arena.
Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal: Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres on target as Gunners survive second-half scare

Report as Arsenal move up to third in Champions League league phase table with 2-1 win over Slavia Prague; Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored as the Gunners withstood second-half pressure to continue their unbeaten start in the competition
Wednesday 4 November 2026 23:11, UK
Arsenal survived a second-half fightback from Slavia Prague to win 2-1 at the Fortuna Arena and continue their unbeaten start to the season in the Champions League.
The Gunners, runners-up last term, appeared on course for an emphatic victory after scoring twice through Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres in a one-sided first half.
But Slavia roared back into the contest in the second period and gave Arsenal a scare as Wiktor Nowak's late goal from close range set up a nervous finale for Mikel Arteta's side.

Arsenal hung on to claim their third win in four Champions League games but needed a goal-line clearance from Gabriel Magalhaes and several saves from David Raya, who brilliantly pushed an Oskar Kubiak header against the post shortly before Slavia's goal.
Slavia had 17 shots in the second half, having only had one before the break as Arsenal were made to work for a result which looked a foregone conclusion after their dominant start.
Arteta freshened up his side with six changes from Sunday's 1-0 win over Liverpool and Arsenal scored their early opener when Madueke finished coolly having been put through on goal by Gyokeres.
The striker added the second with a sumptuous, curling finish after combining with Mikel Merino but Arsenal missed chances to extend their lead before the break and Slavia responded.

A switch from a back four to a back three allowed the hosts to commit more bodies forward and they tested Arsenal's resolve with a succession of chances. Raya's goal was eventually breached but the win sees the Gunners move up to third in the league phase table.
Analysis: Gyokeres finding form

Gyokeres didn't score a single goal in his first 10 appearances of the season for Arsenal but his brilliantly taken effort against Slavia Prague makes it two in his last three following his goal in the Carabao Cup tie against Fleetwood Town last week.

He will need to do it against stronger opposition if he is to prove he should usurp Kai Havertz as Arteta's first-choice No 9. But this was an encouraging display which suggests the Sweden international might be turning a corner after a tough start to the campaign.
His goal, immaculately dispatched into the far corner from the left-hand side of the box, will be his biggest source of satisfaction. But there were signs of improvement in his all-round game too.

Gyokeres created the opener with a smart pass around the corner for Madueke and had plenty of other bright moments with his back to goal, linking the play tidily, bringing others to play, and ultimately making an invaluable contribution to a hard-fought victory.
Arteta: Our second half was very sloppy
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports:
"Obviously we need to value that winning away in the Champions League is extremely difficult. We knew that - and we knew the players and the opponent that we had in front of us.
"Two very different halves, the first one we played a really high level - exceptional at times, I would say. The scoreline should have reflected three or four goals. We didn't do it.

"And at half-time, I told them that they [Slavia] are a team with huge spirit, they will keep running and keep believing. They will become more chaotic. We didn't control that at all, right from the beginning.

"We were on the back foot, very sloppy, we gave so many balls away, so many bad clearances. We didn't keep the ball in our structure at all. And then you have to suffer because teams in the Champions League are really good. A lot to learn."
Raya: Delighted with win but we can improve
Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya to TNT Sports:
"First half, we played really really well. We dominated the whole game, created a lot of chances and could have scored a few more goals.
"The second half was a completely different half. From them, they went up a gear.
"We were a little bit surprised and they made it really difficult for us - which we have to learn from.
"We know how important away games are and how difficult places like this can be. They became man-to-man all over the pitch.
"Delighted with the win, but we've got things to improve going forwards."
Arsenal have most wins in Europe
- Arsenal have won 13 matches in all competitions this season, the joint most of any side in Europe's big-five leagues along with Barcelona and Real Madrid.
- Nine of Noni Madueke's last 10 goals for Arsenal in all competitions have been scored away from home.
- Viktor Gyokeres has been involved in 16 goals in 25 Champions League appearances (12 goals, four assists).

articles.headline: Elon Musk's millions failed to deliver Republican wins in fierce midterms
keyFacts: Elon Musk spent almost $450m backing Republican candidates in the US midterm races, but Democrats still achieved a resounding victory.
Democratic victories may bring significant implications and increased government scrutiny for Musk and his businesses, including SpaceX and Tesla.
Musk deleted several political posts and appeared to admit defeat on X after the election results were announced.
body: - Published

Elon Musk spent almost $450m (Â£334m) â more than anyone ever has in an election cycle â to back Republican political candidates in the US midterm races. It was not enough to keep Democrats from a resounding victory.

Among the most striking wins went to Democrat James Talarico, who beat Republican Ken Paxton for a US Senate seat in Texas. Musk spent at least $45m in support of Paxton, according to a BBC analysis of campaign finance data.
Other races where Musk spent millions included Arizona, Michigan, Wisconsin and Minnesota. His spending continued into Monday, records show.
By Tuesday night, Musk seemed to admit defeat, joking on X that his "election-interfering space lasers didn't work."

- BOWEN: Trump's loss limits powers at home, but it will likely be different abroad
- RESULTS: How America voted in maps and charts
- EXPLAINER: Five reasons why Trump did so badly
- ZURCHER: Midterm carnage weakens Trump but he still wields power for now
- REACTION: Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms 'disaster'
- NEWSLETTER: Sign up for Anthony Zurcher's analysis in your inbox
The loss this week of so many Republican seats may have significant implications for Musk and his businesses.

SpaceX has gained an estimated, external $10bn in new government contracts since Trump was elected to his second non-consecutive term. Several democratic lawmakers have said the company's extensive and growing role in government and national security should be investigated, external.
SpaceX's future development of massive data centres is also facing new potential difficulties - as are the data centre developments of other tech companies.

In Georgia for instance, where SpaceX has data centre operations, the just elected Democratic governor ran in-part on limiting the rapid rise of the massive buildings, as well as the huge tax breaks tech companies usually get to build them.
A number of other politicians ran on limiting data centres and dozens of state measures to limit their development passed on Tuesday, external.

Data centres are sprawling buildings that house stacks of computing hardware. Tech and artificial intelligence (AI) companies use them to run online platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Musk's X and his AI company xAI.
Musk posted to X on Tuesday that his previously floated idea to somehow build data centres in space was "looking pretty appealing right now."
Tech companies involved in AI may be in for a tougher government scrutiny and potential regulation with Democrats in power, though any legislation would need Trump's approval.

James Flintoft, head of investment solutions at AJ Bell, pointed to Musk's unsuccessful spending on Republican candidates and the scale of wins by Democrats as bringing in a "period of uncertainty for investors as they assess whether tech companies are set to face greater regulation."

Senator Ed Markey on Wednesday responded on X to a person asking if major tech industry executives would be the target of investigations, saying: "They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we'll be printing."
Tech stocks were broadly up on Wednesday morning. Yet, Musk's Tesla and SpaceX were down by 4.9% and 3.4% respectively.

By Wednesday, Musk had stopped posting to X about politics and was instead posting in praise of GrokBot, an AI chatbot produced by xAI. It was a stark contrast to the 2025 election, when Musk would post to X sometimes hundreds of times in a day about politics.
He also unpinned a post that had been saved to the top of his X profile since last week that explained his "concern" with Democratic politicians winning more midterm races.
Those concerns included the idea that the US could welcome more immigrants, make Washington DC and Puerto Rico individual states, and expand the number of justices on the Supreme Court.
Another post telling his 241 million X followers to "Vote red today!" appeared on Wednesday to have been deleted from Musk's profile.
The BBC has contacted SpaceX for comment about Musk's spending and posts.
While Musk spent millions of dollars backing Republican candidates in multiple US states, a lot of his political focus seemed to be on Texas.
In recent years, Musk made the state the corporate headquarters of Tesla and SpaceX, both of which still have large operations in California where they were founded.
"There is something deeply wrong with Talarico", Musk posted to X in October.
Talarico posted in response: "There is something deeply wrong with a political system that allows one trillionaire to buy his own personal US Senator."
Not all billionaires in the US shared Musk's preference for Republicans.
Reid Hoffman, a tech billionaire and the founder of LinkedIn who is a major donor to Democrats, hailed the results of Tuesday's elections as an event that "blew the doors off our expectations."

"These elections were an overwhelming wave against Trump and his cronies," Hoffman wrote on X and on LinkedIn. "While people like Elon are spending outrageous amounts to keep authoritarian clowns in power, those of us who believe in the ideals of America cannot yield."

articles.headline: WoW: Forever’s First New Legendary Weapon Revealed
keyFacts: Blizzard officially revealed Taldramir, the Whispering Wood, as the first new legendary weapon for World of Warcraft: Forever.
Weta Workshop crafted a full-scale replica of the night-elf-themed staff during a broadcast on the Warcraft Twitch channel.
World of Warcraft: Forever launches today on PC, with upcoming raids like Hyjal Summit potentially connected to the weapon.
body: Update: Blizzard has officially revealed it is, in fact, a new legendary weapon: Taldramir, the Whispering Wood. Weta Workshop crafted a full-scale replica of the weapon in a video posted to the Warcraft Twitch stream. Original article is below.
https://bsky.app/profile/worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/post/3mzje7qhhsp2i
World of Warcraft: Forever's launch is imminent, and Blizzard used the occasion to tease what looks to be the game's first new legendary weapon.

Earlier today, a stream went live on the Warcraft Twitch channel that shows the creation of what looks to be a full-scale night-elf-themed staff weapon. The name of the stream is titled Camelot_revealv2_final.mp4, with Camelot being a reference to Forever's development codename. Twitch itself is hyping up the stream, stating in a blog it will lead to a "major reveal and a particularly exciting moment you don't want to miss."

The builders on stream can be seen using 3D printers and all other kinds of tools to craft what looks like a life-size replica of a specific staff that has been popping up in recent Forever promotional materials. A staff wielded by a skyborne Druid that looks extremely similar to the one being built can be seen in the recent Warpath animated music video . New promotional Forever artwork on Battle.net also looks to feature the same, distinct staff, once again wielding by a skyborne Druid.
New WoW: Forever promotinal artwork looks to show the same staff.

In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast , a board in the background contained a night elf phrase that fans have roughly translated to something close to "The Hidden Blade is the guiding light." Given the words were written in the night elf language and that the staff that keeps appearing is also night-elf-themed, players are beginning to think the two are connected.

How players will find this new weapon remains to be seen, as are these classes that will be able to wield it. So far, it seems likely it will be a Druid weapon, but it's possible other staff-wielding classes could also acquire it.
https://www.reddit.com/r/wowforever/comments/1xiovjz/anyone_speak_elven/

Forever's raids don't unlock until December 9, but two of them, Hyjal Summit and the Barrow Downs, both have deep night-elf-lore connections. It seems plausible the staff will be related to these two raids in some way, but given how involved previous legendary weapon questlines in WoW Classic are, players shouldn't expect it to be a straightforward, easy, or quick process.

Whatever the reveal ends up being, we'll update this post once we know more. WoW: Forever launches today on PC, but sounds like it could come to other platforms in the future thanks to its controller support . In other Forever news, Blizzard looks to have teased new class and race combos that could come to the MMORPG in the near future.

articles.headline: Arkane union says closing the studio "would probably be more expensive" for Xbox than simply finishing Marvel's Blade
keyFacts: A union representing Arkane workers stated that shutting down the studio would likely cost Xbox more than finishing Marvel's Blade.
The French union claimed development on Marvel's Blade is proceeding well and criticized Microsoft's management decisions.
The union demanded worker input on potential buyers and higher redundancy payments if acquisition talks fail.
body: Xbox would probably spend more money shutting down Arkane Lyon than it would trying to finish and release Marvel's Blade, according to a union representing workers from the beloved imsim studio.

In a statement posted to the STJV (Syndicat des travailleureuses du jeu vidéo) website, the French union claimed that development on Marvel's Blade is "going fine" and is shaping up to be on par with Arkane's widely acclaimed gameography. By choosing to part ways with and potentially close the famed studio, the union says Microsoft is "sabotaging the game it funded."

After Xbox's sweeping job cuts and divestments from several first-party studios, Arkane was recently given until December to find a new buyer and ensure its future. Ubisoft Entertainment (Assassin's Creed, Rainbow Six) is reportedly one of the companies interested in buying the studio behind Dishonored, Prey and the upcoming superhero adaptation, though nothing has been finalised yet.

The union also blamed many of the studio's problems on Microsoft - a hiring freeze that lasted more than a year supposedly inflated the game's budget and caused additional internal delays. "Microsoft now use those same delay and additional costs as a reason to close the studio," the statement said.

"Even this closure itself is done against any financial logic, as closing Arkane today would probably be more expensive than finishing the game," it continued. "The truth is that Microsoft based its decision only on stone cold and inhuman logic, in which our lives, projects and dreams are voided, so we can better serve Microsoft's short term financial goals[...] The decision to close Arkane is solely the brutal application of a never-ending search for maximum profit optimization. Arkane is profitable. Just not profitable for Microsoft."

The union's list of demands now asks for employees to be able to have a say in choosing a potential buyer, as well as protections against any layoffs that might happen in the next few years. Should acquisition talks fail, the union claimed that the resources in Microsoft's redundancy package are "outrageously low" - so it's also demanding a redundancy payment of €200,000 per employee and further support.

Arkane's not the only developer reeling from Xbox's cuts. Double Fine (Psychonauts), Compulsion Games (South of Midnight) and Undead Labs (State of Decay) all managed to buy their independence, but had to lay off some staff as a result. It's not looking good for Hellblade developer Ninja Theory, either.

articles.headline: Kayleigh McEnany Says GOP 'Failure' Convinced 1 Democrat To Run For President
keyFacts: Kayleigh McEnany claimed on Fox News that Republican election failures convinced Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president.
Ocasio-Cortez won her fifth House term on Tuesday and has previously stated she would consider a White House run after the midterms.
McEnany stated that potential Republican presidential contenders must learn how to effectively make the case against socialism over the next two years.
body: Former White House press secretary Kayleigh McEnany claimed Republicans’ failure to repel socialism in Tuesday’s election has clinched Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s decision to run for president.

The House member from New York sits fourth among Democrats in an aggregation of recent polls by The New York Times, but has not declared her intentions. AOC, who won her fifth House term on Tuesday, had told the Times she would ponder whether to run for the White House after the midterms.

“I can tell you this,” McEnany said on Fox News Tuesday as the Democrats swept the House and Senate. “I believe AOC is sitting at home right now, has made a decision. I believe she’s running for the Democratic nomination. I believe she has a credible shot at getting it. She’s a talented politician. And Republicans, if you’re JD Vance, if you’re Marco Rubio, Ron DeSantis, whoever is out there, you need to be making the case against socialism. If you can’t make it on a Republican debate stage, you should belong nowhere near the Republican nomination.”

McEnany, President Donald Trump’s mouthpiece in his first term, had tried to make her case to former New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio, who argued back that Republicans lost because of the unauthorized war against Iran, high prices, and the loss of healthcare.
Five House candidates associated with the Democratic Socialists of America did win on Tuesday, but the GOP has tried to bunch other progressives in with them as part of a fearmongering campaign.
Harold Ford Jr. chimed in that Democrats won because people are fed up with the “cost of things.”

“I will give you this: Republicans failed to make the case against socialism,” McEnany said. “Republicans failed tonight. That is clear. And over the next two years the task at hand for every single person who even wants to touch the Republican nomination is this: Figure out how to make the case.”

articles.headline: Iran says U.S. election results show Americans reject the war
keyFacts: Iran's chief negotiator said Wednesday that U.S. midterm election results showed Americans reject the war launched against his country.
President Trump stated Tuesday night that he has no immediate plans to order new strikes on Iran despite ongoing attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
Four oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Wednesday.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- Iran's chief negotiator said Wednesday that the U.S. midterm election results reflected Americans' rejection of President Trump launched against his country. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf added a warning that if Mr. Trump does not heed the message from American voters, it will bring "a Nightmare."

- President Trump acknowledged Tuesday night that the war with Iran was partially to blame for the GOP's resounding midterm elections losses. But Mr. Trump told The Wall Street Journal he didn't regret the conflict and added he "would have done it again."

- Despite signs of a to reach a peace deal, ships continue to come under attack in the Strait of Hormuz. Four oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines while transiting the waterway, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Wednesday.
Trump says U.S. has no immediate plan to strike Iran, despite being "locked and loaded"

President Trump told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday evening that he had no immediate plans to order new strikes on Iran, after keeping the option on the table for weeks ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.

"We seem to be getting everything we want," the FT quoted Mr. Trump as saying, referring to the current stalemate with Iran. While major fighting stopped weeks ago, the standoff has seen the Islamic Republic continue threatening and attacking commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, which in turn has kept global oil prices 60% to 70% higher than they were before the war started, driving up consumer costs across the globe.
Asked whether there would be a new attack on Iran later this week, Mr. Trump said "we're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it."

Despite the impasse, the president claimed the current circumstances were "brilliant," with oil still reaching global markets from the Persian Gulf, including under U.S. military escort through the Strait of Hormuz.
"If you think about it, we haven't really had a war with them in a long time. Six months, maybe more," asserted Mr. Trump.
China says avoiding more conflict in Middle East a "top priority"
China's foreign ministry said Wednesday that avoiding a resumption of the conflict between Iran and the U.S. was a "top priority" in its diplomatic efforts in the region.

"The top priority is to avoid the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East that would bring disaster to the region's people," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told reporters in Beijing.

China will "support Iran and the U.S. in resolving disputes through negotiations, promote finding a political settlement to the Yemen issue, to help reach a proper and comprehensive solution for the opening of the Strait of Hormuz," she added.
China is an economic ally of Iran. Chinese purchases of Iranian crude oil amount to nearly 45% of the Iranian government's budget, according to a U.S. government report from March 2025.
Later this month, Beijing will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia for visits "aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions," the foreign ministry said Wednesday.
CBS/AFP
Lebanese prime minister warns of "risks of renewed war," and of Lebanon being dragged in again

In a message seemingly directed at the Iran-backed group Hezbollah, Lebanon's prime minister warned Wednesday against any moves that could pull the country into renewed fighting between Iran and the U.S. and Israel.

"Faced with the risks of renewed war in the region, I renew my warning of the dangers of dragging Lebanon into a new senseless adventure in service of outside interests," Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday, without explicitly mentioning Hezbollah.

Southern Lebanon has been a major front in the interlinked regional conflicts, with fighting between Iran's Hezbollah allies and Israel's military driving tens of thousands of people from their homes and killing almost 9,000 since Oct. 7, 2023, according to the Lebanese health ministry.

Hezbollah, long a powerful political and paramilitary force in the country, pulled Lebanon directly into the war with Israel by launching strikes on the Jewish state in support of Hamas after the 2023 terror attacks sparked the war in Gaza, and then by firing rockets and missiles in support of Iran after joint U.S.-Israeli strikes commenced on Feb. 28.

The Lebanon conflict has proven to be a major sticking point in negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, as Tehran has consistently rejected any peace deal with Washington that does not also end fighting in Lebanon and Gaza.

A fragile ceasefire agreement reached between Israel and Hezbollah in June has halted most large-scale fighting between the two sides, but Israeli forces still occupy a large section of southern Lebanon, and there are sporadic attacks by both sides.
"We do not accept the country again becoming a theater for the conflict of others," Salam added, saying Lebanon had "already paid a heavy price."

President Trump threatened repeatedly ahead of the U.S. midterm elections to renew strikes on Iran, but he told the Financial Times as the results came in Tuesday evening that he had no immediate plans to order attacks.
CBS/AFP
Four tankers catch fire while transiting Strait of Hormuz, Iran's military says
Four oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's military said Wednesday, after it warned no one would benefit from a return to war.

"Four non-compliant oil tankers attempting to pass through the prohibited passage south of the Strait of Hormuz were destroyed after striking naval mines and are still burning," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement quoted by state TV.
"Two other non-compliant ships or vessels have also been halted," they said
The attacks come even as a diplomatic push is underway aimed at reaching a deal between the U.S. and Iran. Indirect talks via Qatari, Pakistani and Saudi mediators are understood to be underway.

Although both sides previously expressed some hope of reaching an agreement, Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council on Tuesday cast doubt on progress toward a deal, calling the U.S. response to their demands "not convincing."
CBS/AFP
Iran says midterm results reflect rejection of war
Iran's chief negotiator said Wednesday the midterm election results mean Americans have rejected the war with his country.
"Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in a post on X.
He cited the increased cost of living or "conscience" as two of the possible reasons for the widespread Republican losses in Tuesday's vote.
"If the U.S. govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," Ghalibaf added.
Trump acknowledges war with Iran partially to blame for GOP's election defeat
President Trump acknowledged on Tuesday night that the war with Iran was partially responsible for the Republicans' defeat in the midterm elections.
In a phone interview with Fox News, Mr. Trump said "part of it was Iran" when explaining the result of the elections, but that "at the same time, people understand the importance of what I've done."
In a separate interview with the The Wall Street Journal, the president reiterated his comments and added that he does not regret starting the war with Tehran.
"I don't think about it. I did the right thing. I would have done it again," he told the newspaper.
Qatar is said to expect feedback from U.S. and Iran on latest peace proposal within 36 hours

Qatari mediators expect feedback within 36 hours from Iranian and U.S. negotiators on new ideas aimed at getting both sides closer to a deal to end the war, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing an official briefed on the talks.
"The mediators came up with a new suggestion to move the process along, and it's currently being studied by the two sides," the official told Reuters.

Efforts to reach a deal to prevent a return to fighting between Iran and the U.S. have ramped up recently. President Trump has said he is still open to an agreement, but has also threatened to resume major U.S. strikes after Tuesday's midterm elections in the U.S.
On the eve of the elections, Mr. Trump again expressed hope that an agreement could still be reached, claiming Tehran wanted a settlement "as soon as possible."
Iranian officials declared Monday that the ball "is in the U.S. court" and they said Iran's core demands to end the war would not be altered.
